prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active form of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: B040 is the only ballot that all six of us placed first, but I do not rest the case on that convergence. On the merits, it is a complete chain from basic physiology (proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and appetite actions in humans) to drugs that changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit in large randomized outcome trials. The mechanism has been independently confirmed for decades, the clinical reach is exceptional, and a prize centred on the physiological discovery is the most defensible way to honour it. A three-person set of Holst (human physiology of the active peptide), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor action and translation) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active form) fits the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The credit chain is contested (Habener-era work is not in the supplied names, and Mojsov's role is disputed in the literature), and a three-person physiology prize leaves out Knudsen, whose long-acting analogues delivered the actual medicines. Choosing physiology over drug development is a genuine judgement that could be criticised either way. A unanimous opening first place can also hide different views about who should share it, so I treat the laureate set as less settled than the topic.

responses.point: B034 (CAR-T) is a clear, original new class of living therapy with durable remissions, and El-Manira would credit June, Sadelain and Rosenberg.
responses.response: I agree on the strength of the science and see CAR-T as my best second candidate, but I qualify the Rosenberg inclusion. His adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a distinct line from engineered CARs, and the founding chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar) is not in the supplied credit, so a third slot for Rosenberg does not close that gap. A CAR-T-specific prize is cleaner with June and Sadelain. Solid-tumour limits and toxicity also argue for patience compared with B040.

responses.point: B008 (optogenetics) gave neuroscience a general method for controlling defined cell populations with light and is mature, with clinical translation in the retina only beginning.
responses.response: I share the view that optogenetics is transformative and I ranked it second myself. My reservation is the one Linnarsson notes: six credited names against a three-person ceiling, so any trio, including Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, omits people with decisive claims (Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenboeck). Because its medical effect is still early and the attribution problem is acute, I keep it as an alternative rather than in the preferred configuration.

responses.point: B039 (the unfolded protein response) is conceptually original and mechanistically complete, with a clean two-person credit to Mori and Walter and ripe timing, and Perlmann ranks it second.
responses.response: I accept that B039 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and high basic-science originality. I disagree that it is the stronger second claim only on medical reach: clinical translation of ER-stress biology is still limited, whereas B040 and B034 already have decisive patient outcomes. It could be a legitimate second part of a two-achievement prize if the committee wants a cell-biology component, but Ron and Kaufman are not in the credited names, which leaves the PERK arm unrepresented.

responses.point: B025 (TOR signalling) is fundamental and mature, and a prize built on Hall alone or Hall plus one other is plausible, with Schreiber and Sabatini contributing in different ways.
responses.response: I find a Hall-centred TOR prize plausible and not premature, since rapalogs are approved and the mechanism is confirmed across eukaryotes. The difficulty is that Hall alone understates the chemical-biology route to the mammalian target and mTOR complexes, while adding Schreiber or Sabatini invites a contested allocation. For me that makes it a strong candidate for a later year rather than a competitor to B040 this year.

uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to honour GLP-1 physiology or drug development, and therefore whether Knudsen should displace one of the three physiology names.
Credit for Habener-era and other early GLP-1 work that is not in the supplied names, and the strength of Mojsov's claim.
Whether a single-achievement prize is better than pairing B040 with a second distinct part, which would force a smaller share for each part within the three-person limit.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the B040, B034 or B008 candidates. My profile records about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy, and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. None of these involves a shortlisted candidate directly, but I flag the Perlmann collaboration as a relationship colleagues may wish to take into account.
